label: Assumption audit
title: Assumptions and derived conclusions

checks.claim: The target is \(\Pi_N\propto e^{-V_N}\), with \(V_N(z)=\sum_iU(\theta,\sqrt N z^i)\).
checks.note: The target is the actual lifted Gibbs measure; the LSI hypothesis includes probability normalization.

checks.claim: The parameter noise is \(\sqrt{2\gamma/N}\), while physical particle noise is \(\sqrt{2\gamma}\).
checks.note: Exact coordinate update identities and the independent-Gaussian law identity connect the canonical Markov laws to the existing noise-driven implementation.

checks.claim: The lifted dimension is \(D=d_\theta+Nd_x\), and base smoothness \(L\) gives lifted smoothness \(NL\).
checks.note: The quadratic replicated-pair identity gives the gradient bound. Strong convexity is not needed for these identities or the LSI endpoint.

checks.claim: The actual lifted target satisfies \(2\beta H\le J\) with \(\beta>0\).
checks.note: The only functional inequality premise is IsLogSobolev for the actual lifted target. A pair-target LSI is not substituted for this premise.

checks.claim: For \(D>0\), \(\beta\le NL\) follows from LSI and smoothness; \(0<\gamma\le\beta/(4NL^2)\) is the positive step restriction.
checks.note: In positive lifted dimension, the shared compatibility theorem proves beta <= N L from the actual target LSI and smoothness. Singleton state spaces are handled separately. The positive step restriction remains the stated algorithmic hypothesis.

checks.claim: At every positive interpolation time, the constructed density satisfies \(\rho_t=r_t\Pi_N\), where \(\rho_t\) is the law of the actual frozen-drift Gaussian step.
checks.note: The actual frozen Gaussian law is identified with its explicit positive mixture density at every positive time; its relative density is constructed with respect to the normalized Gibbs target.

checks.claim: The actual entropy is absolutely continuous on compact positive-time intervals and satisfies the proved entropy identity almost everywhere.
checks.note: Exact kernel time derivatives and Gaussian Fisher bounds give local spacetime integrability. Bounded logarithmic entropy tests yield an integrated identity; dominated limits prove actual entropy is locally absolutely continuous with its flux as derivative almost everywhere.

checks.claim: The actual Gaussian flux satisfies the spatial weak identity, and bounded entropy tests converge to the full entropy-production identity.
checks.note: The explicit Gaussian flux satisfies the actual weak equation. Bounded entropy tests are admitted by integrability and global integration by parts; their limit supplies the full entropy identity without assuming an unbounded test is admissible.

checks.claim: For the actual frozen update \(Y_t\), \(\mathbb E\|\nabla V_N(Y_t)-\nabla V_N(X)\|^2\le t^2(NL)^2G_k+2tD(NL)^2\).
checks.note: The exact Gaussian displacement energy and gradient Lipschitzness give the frozen-gradient error energy. The actual pair law equals the Gaussian-weighted Lebesgue pair density, preserving the sharp constants in the entropy calculation.

A Gibbs squared-score exponential moment and the entropy inequality prove integrability and G <= 4 ell H + 2 D ell directly. Derived beta <= ell gives the coefficient 4 ell^2/beta. No transport-entropy premise is needed.
Finite initial KL is the initial-law hypothesis. The unconditional shared theorem proves every iterated output KL finite before taking its real value; no regular interpolation data are required.
Actual entropy production, the original LSI, the derived moment bound, and scalar comparison give the recurrence. The forcing substitution cancels both particle factors from the squared step.
The shared unconditional ULA theorem and exact lift yield the full joint estimate. Geometric summation gives constant 8; output finiteness is retained.
Divide the proved full-state real entropy bound by positive N, including both its initial contribution and bias. The unnormalized KL finiteness witness is retained.

checks.claim: If \(\beta=N\alpha\), the normalized bias is \((8\gamma L^2/\alpha)(d_x+d_\theta/N)\) and the rate is \(e^{-\alpha\gamma k}\).
checks.status: proved under the actual lifted LSI of strength N alpha
checks.note: The lifted-target functional inequality with constant N alpha is explicitly assumed. Exact scaling gives the step gamma <= alpha/(4L^2), rate exp(-alpha gamma k), and intensive dimension dx+dtheta/N.

checks.claim: Parameter KL is at most full joint KL; a bound \(H_k/N\le B\) gives parameter KL at most \(NB\).
checks.note: The unconditional finite-initial-KL wrapper projects the actual joint law. Marginal KL is finite and bounded by full joint KL; normalization by N is not applied to the parameter divergence.

checks.claim: The proved conclusion concerns sampling error in relative entropy.
checks.note: Neither LSI scaling alone nor normalized joint entropy supplies concentration around a marginal-likelihood maximizer. No optimization or MMLE error estimate is claimed in this extension.

verdict: The actual Gaussian IPLA entropy theorem is proved from differentiability, gradient Lipschitzness, an LSI for the actual lifted Gibbs target, the positive admissible step, and finite initial joint KL. The shared ULA proof constructs the density, entropy chain rule, initial entropy boundary, moments, compatibility, and recurrence. The older RegularInterpolationData theorems remain reusable interfaces; they are not inputs to the unconditional endpoint. No pair-to-lift LSI transfer or optimizer concentration is inferred.
